Action.description: A command: `[verify]`, and the command part of a production.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the evidence file. Defaults to its directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the program.

stdin.description: File fed to the program's standard input (relative to the evidence file).

stdout.description: Write the program's standard output to the main output.

timeout.description: Kill the program after this long (default: `execution.timeout` from the config).

Claim.description: A claim: a range of the subject and the references it relates to.

broad.description:
Why this claim's range, or a range it references, is broad on purpose (`[coverage]`
of the configuration says when a range is broad). Acknowledged broad ranges are still
reported and still left out of narrow coverage.

evidence.description: References the range relates to (at least one).

note.description: Free-form note (reasoning, caveats). Part of the definition.

select.description: The range of the subject this claim is about.

author.description:
Who writes the subject, e.g. `human` or `ai:claude`. Descriptive only: it changes
nothing about how the subject is updated or pinned.

claims.description: Hand-written claims: ranges of the subject and the references they relate to.

format.description: Subject format. Inferred from the subject's extension when omitted.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the project.

members.description:
Makes the subject a list (a JSON array or JSONL) whose entries are kept as member
pairs, each generated from a template and updated on its own.

primary.description: Ranges of the subject declared as primary information (no evidence required).

productions.description:
Commands that produce the subject and/or claims. Without a production that writes
the subject, the subject is edited directly (editable).

requirements.description: Requirements this subject defines (for requirement coverage).

schema.description: Schema every new version of the subject must conform to.

scope.description:
The parts of the subject that coverage counts. Without an including entry the whole
subject counts; entries with `exclude = true` then remove parts (front matter, chapters
that nothing depends on).

storage.description: Storage policy for new snapshots of this subject.

subject.description:
Where the subject lives: a path relative to this evidence file's directory, or
absolute. Defaults to this file's own path without `.evid` (the sidecar layout). A
subject outside the project works, but draws a `subject-outside-project` warning.

tags.description: Free-form tags for search and grouping.

verify.description: Optional check run on every new version of the subject before it is adopted.

wiki.description:
How the subject appears in a wiki (`evidence-wiki`): other names, categories, and the
kind of page. Evidence itself does not read it.

oneOf.description: JSON Lines (one JSON value per line); schemas apply to each line.

anyOf.description: A fixed value; placeholders except `{env.NAME}` are expanded.
A command (no shell) whose trimmed standard output is the value.

LocatorValue.description: A locator entry: a value or a command printing the value.

Member.description: A member of a list. Its definition is composed from the parent's `[members]` template and the list entry; any other evidence file field overrides the template for this member only.

member.description: Key of this member's entry in the parent's list.

member_of.description: Id of the parent evidence, whose subject is the list.

id.description: Id of each member, e.g. `space-{member.id}`. Use the key field so ids stay stable.

key.description:
JSON Pointer to the stable key of each list entry, e.g. `/id`. Members are matched to
entries by this key, so a member keeps its history when other fields change.

on_removed.description: What `evidence update` does with a member that is no longer listed. Default `keep`.

subject.description:
Subject of each member, relative to this evidence file's directory, e.g.
`pages/{member.path}.md`. The member's evidence file is the sidecar of its subject.

template.description:
Definition shared by every member: any evidence file field except `version`, `id`,
`subject`, `members`, and `state`. Strings may use `{member.FIELD}` (a top-level text,
number, or boolean field of the entry).

OnRemoved.description: What happens to a member that is no longer listed.

oneOf.description: Keep it and report `member-removed` until its definition is removed.
Delete it, unless other evidence depends on it (then keep it and report it).
The complete set of claims of the production's namespace (`{claims}`).

PageKind.description: The kind of a wiki page.

oneOf.description: A category page: lists the pages that name it in `categories`.
A term (glossary) page: explains a word used across several pages.

Primary.description: A range declared as primary information (`[[primary]]`).

select.description: The range (`{ whole = true }` for the whole subject).

Production.description:
A production: a command that writes the subject, claims, or both (`[[productions]]`).

Evidence runs commands; it has no built-in knowledge of any data source. The program runs
without a shell; placeholders such as `{output}`, `{claims}`, and `{input.NAME}` are
expanded in `run`, `env`, `cwd`, `stdin`, and `locator` (see `docs/format-v2.md`).

acquisition.description:
Whether this subject writer retrieves external data. Defaults to true for inputless
subject writers. Set false for jobs that generate original content.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the evidence file. Defaults to its directory.

env.description: Extra environment variables for the program.

inputs.description:
Evidence the command reads. A change of an input's selected content is a reason to
re-run the production.

interval.description:
Minimum time between runs by a plain `evidence update`. Without it, the production
runs only when something changed or when requested.

locator.description:
Where the content came from, recorded after each successful run: a fixed value
(placeholders expanded) or a command whose trimmed standard output is the value.

name.description: Stable name, unique within the file. Records are kept per name.

namespace.description:
Claim namespace (required when `writes` has `claims`): the production owns every
claim id starting with `<namespace>.`.

reconstruct.description:
Optional acquisition command for rebuilding a published version. Uses the same execution
settings as `run` and can expand `{locator.KEY}` in its arguments.

stdin.description: File fed to the program's standard input (relative to the evidence file).

stdout.description:
Write the program's standard output to the main output: `{output}` when the
production writes the subject, else `{claims}`.

timeout.description: Kill the program after this long (default: `execution.timeout` from the config).

writes.description: What the production writes: `["subject"]`, `["claims"]`, or both.

anyOf.description: Evidence id (the whole subject, current version).
Evidence id with a range, a version, or options.

Reference.description: A reference to evidence: in a claim's `evidence`, or a production's `inputs`.

as.description: Inputs only: name used in placeholders (`{input.<name>}`); defaults to the id.

path.description: For directory subjects: path of the file inside the directory.

revision.description: A fixed version (`sha256:…`). Without it, the reference follows the current version.

satisfies.description:
Claims only: id of the requirement (declared by the referenced evidence) that this
reference satisfies.

select.description: Part of the referenced subject; only changes of this part count.

Requirement.description: A requirement defined by this subject (`[[requirements]]`).

id.description: Stable id, unique within the file.

select.description: The range of the subject stating the requirement.

json_schema.description: Path to a JSON Schema, relative to the evidence file.

Scope.description: A part of the subject that coverage counts, or (with `exclude`) leaves out (`[[scope]]`).

exclude.description: Leave the part out of coverage instead of counting it.

note.description: Free-form note (why the part counts or does not).

path.description:
For directory subjects: a file, or a directory (every file under it), inside the
subject. Without it the entry is about every file.

select.description: The range of each file the entry is about. Without it, whole files.

Selector.description: Names a part of a document.

oneOf.description: A Markdown section by heading text. Leading `#`s, if given, also constrain the level.
Lines between a `span:NAME` marker line and a `/span:NAME` marker line.

SnapshotIdSchema.description: Content id: `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters.

StoragePolicy.description: Per-evidence snapshot encryption policy. An omitted setting inherits from dependencies.

encryption.description: `true` encrypts the subject. `false` permits plaintext with plaintext dependencies.

WikiPage.description:
How a subject appears in a wiki (`[wiki]`).

Every pair is a page of the wiki. This table only adds what the evidence file does not say
already: the title, description, and tags are the evidence file's own.

aliases.description: Other names the page is found and linked by (`[[alias]]` links to it).

categories.description:
Categories the page belongs to. Each names a category page by its title, an alias, or
its id, the same way a `[[link]]` does; a category without a page is *wanted*.

hidden.description: Leave the page out of navigation, listings, and search (it can still be linked).

kind.description: What the page is. Defaults to `article`.

description: Evidence file (format version 2) defining a subject, how it is produced, and its claims. Usually a sidecar `<subject>.evid` next to the subject; `subject` places the subject elsewhere.
title: Evidence file
